headline: How product teams turn behavioral data into daily decisions
deck: A fictional Amplitude Daily brief for demo readers evaluating analytics and experimentation.
body: Product leaders no longer wait for quarterly reviews to understand what changed in their funnels. They compare cohorts, session paths, and retention curves every morning—then ship answers the same day.
This article is seeded content from Phase 0. Search, topics, and recommendations build on this route in Phase 1.
author: maya-chen

headline: Five retention myths that skew experiment results
deck: Why naive day-N curves mislead teams before they instrument properly.
body: Teams often declare victory when short-term engagement spikes, even if the cohort never returns. Retention questions need stable identity and consistent event definitions.
Use holdouts and clear primary metrics before scaling a winning variant across surfaces.
author: jordan-lee

headline: Finding funnel friction without drowning in charts
deck: A practical order of operations for PMs auditing drop-off.
body: Start with the business question, then map steps that mirror user intent—not org chart handoffs.
Pair funnel views with session replay on the worst step to separate UX bugs from expectation gaps.
author: maya-chen

headline: When to stop an experiment early (and when not to)
deck: Guardrails for peeking, power, and shipping.
body: Peeking without correction inflates false positives. Pre-register the minimum runtime and success metric before traffic arrives.
Stopping early is appropriate for clear harm guardrails—not because Tuesday looked good.
author: jordan-lee
